floppy_disk.retrotron-welcome.readme:
WELCOME TO YOUR RETROTRON COMPUTER

Congratulations on your purchase. Or on finding this computer on the street.

Your RetroTron can:
- Look for jobs on WorkNet 98
- Receive e-mails, some of them good
- Read floppy disks like this one

To install programs, insert a disk and open SETUP.EXE.
To remove a disk, press the button next to the drive.
To feel productive, rearrange your desktop icons.

Thank you for choosing RetroTron.
We did not really give you a choice.
floppy_disk.minefield.label: Minefield 1.0
floppy_disk.minefield.readme:
MINEFIELD 1.0

A game of logic, patience and pretending to work.

HOW TO PLAY
- Click a field to uncover it.
- Numbers tell you how many mines touch that field.
- Right-click to plant a flag on a mine.
- Uncover every safe field to win.

If your boss walks by, minimize the window.
If your boss plays too, ask for a raise.

landing.tagline: Start your computer. Get a job. Survive office life.
landing.meta_title: DeskLife 98 - retro office simulation in your browser
landing.meta_description: Start with a slow home computer and almost no money, find a job through WorkNet 98 and build a life in a simulated city. A late nineties office simulation that runs in the browser.
landing.hero_title: One computer. One job. One life.
landing.hero_lead: You have little money, a slow machine and no plan. Order a computer and get started.
landing.catalogue_note: Next working day delivery. Please complete the order form in full.
landing.returning_hint: Ordered before? Enter the same address and we will send you the way back to your machine.
landing.about_body: DeskLife 98 is a life and economy simulation experienced entirely through computer screens. You sit in front of a cheap home computer that boots slowly and cannot do much. Through the job portal WorkNet 98 you apply to companies that exist only inside this game. Get hired and you are given a work computer with its own software, and the job begins.
landing.loop_body: The work is made of real small workflows, not yes or no dialogs. A customer reports a burst pipe, you find a free technician in the calendar, book the appointment and confirm it by mail. Meanwhile a colleague writes in the messenger telling you to ignore the mail from the boss. Appointments run by themselves, so you never have to be online at a particular time. Good work earns a bonus and a promotion, bad work earns warnings.
landing.world_body: Behind the companies lies a simulated city with households, people and businesses. Water damage at a resident becomes a job for the plumber, who needs a spare part that a carrier has to deliver. If the delivery is late the appointment fails and somebody complains. These chains keep running while you are away, and any position in them can be held by another player.
landing.money_body: Your salary is not a score. A faster processor shortens boot and loading times, new floppy disks bring new programs, and over time your desk fills up with things you earned yourself. Rent, electricity and the phone bill are still charged every month.
landing.access_body: DeskLife 98 runs in the browser with nothing to install. There is no password: you give an e-mail address and get a sign-in link whenever you come back. The minimum age is 16. The game is in development and currently in a closed test phase.
landing.footer_note: DeskLife 98 is a game set in a fictional world. All companies, brands, people and prices are invented.
legal.placeholder: This text is still missing and has to be filled in before the first external tester.
